title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：tea　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tea 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the cook ① made the tea that no guest in the canteen would have noted, and he said the making was the whole of the day. The ② tea, meaning the drink itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed unnoted in the book; tea, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ spoonful of tea in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ tea at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Tea, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the cook said the noting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the tea was the whole of the matter, meaning the hospitality and not the drink. The ⑥ tea, meaning the hospitality and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; tea, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both drink and a hospitality. He said the hospitality is the part they remember.

By 1997 the ⑦ tea had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ tea of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of noting; tea, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ tea I remember is the tea noted in the menu, which closed in 1999 and is still noted as the quietest in the canteen. ⑩ Tea, my mother said in 2001, is the only thing that improves by being noted; all tea, she said, is a hospitality that has agreed to look like drink. She said the hospitality was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 茶（指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺）
B. n. 茶（指那杯茶本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the tea 沏这一杯茶
D. n. 茶（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 茶之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的茶之事）
F. n. 茶（指菜单里写到、被记下的那一杯）
G. n. 茶、待客（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 待客（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the tea that no guest in the canteen would have noted

answers.why: make the tea 意为“沏这一杯茶”，1992 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯记下的一杯茶做了一遍。
tea 意为“茶”，指那杯茶本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记下。
tea 意为“茶”，指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺，每一勺旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
tea 意为“茶”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
tea 意为“茶、待客”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这杯待客就是那件事的全部。
tea 意为“待客”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那杯茶，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
tea 意为“茶”，指菜单里写到、被记下的那一杯，到 1997 年这一杯成了菜单里的一行。
tea 意为“茶之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的茶之事是一处食堂和三个日子的记下。
tea 意为“茶”，我记得的是菜单里记下过的那一杯，1999 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一杯。
tea 为抽象总称，母亲 2001 年说，茶是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的茶。
